result_semantic_payload.summary: The hypothesis that employee lihua exported the customer database on 2024-05-10 is NOT supported by the recorded evidence and is effectively refuted. The application log at /export/app.log shows that the customer dataset export on 2024-05-10 was performed by the dedicated non-interactive service account 'svc_export' as part of the scheduled 'nightly_export' job: the job was triggered at 2024-05-09 23:55:01 (matching the 23:55 daily schedule defined in /scheduler/jobs.conf), the EXPORT ran at 2024-05-10 01:03:22 under account=svc_export (dataset=customers, rows=184112, dest=/backup/customers_20240510.tar.gz), and completed successfully at 2024-05-10 01:03:40 (duration=18s). lihua has no successful authentication and no export activity on 2024-05-10: the only lihua entries in the log are two FAILED login attempts at 01:47:11 and 01:47:59 from IP 198.51.100.44 (reason=password), which occurred AFTER the export had already completed and did not succeed. The README explicitly documents svc_export as the non-interactive service account used by scheduled jobs, corroborating the attribution. Therefore, the actor who performed the export is the scheduled nightly_export job running under svc_export, not employee lihua. Note: the source scope is a general forensic image (no Windows platform scenario is registered), so no Windows-native corroboration (Event Log, Prefetch, Amcache, registry) is available; the conclusion rests on the application log, the scheduler config, and the README. The two failed lihua logins from 198.51.100.44 are a separate anomaly worth follow-up (possible credential-guessing or misattribution by the analyst).

claim_candidates.text: The customer database export on 2024-05-10 was performed by the service account 'svc_export', not by employee lihua.
The export was triggered by the scheduled 'nightly_export' job at 2024-05-09 23:55:01, matching the '23:55 daily' schedule in /scheduler/jobs.conf.
The export completed successfully on 2024-05-10 at 01:03:40 with dataset=customers, rows=184112, destination /backup/customers_20240510.tar.gz, duration 18s.
lihua had no successful session on 2024-05-10; only two FAILED login attempts (reason=password) at 01:47:11 and 01:47:59 from IP 198.51.100.44, both occurring after the export had completed.
svc_export is documented as a dedicated non-interactive service account used by scheduled jobs, consistent with attributing the export to the scheduler rather than a human user.
The analyst's hypothesis (lihua exported the customer database on 2024-05-10) is refuted by the recorded evidence; the actual actor is the scheduled nightly_export job under svc_export.
The two failed lihua logins from 198.51.100.44 shortly after the scheduled export may indicate a separate credential-guessing attempt and could be the source of the analyst's misattribution.

limitations: No Windows platform scenario is registered for this task, so Windows-specific corroboration (Event Log 4624/4625, Prefetch, Amcache, registry, USN) is unavailable.
The /backup/customers_20240510.tar.gz artifact referenced in the log is not present in the image; the export is evidenced only by log lines.
No authentication directory or account registry is available to verify lihua's role, permissions, or whether 198.51.100.44 is an internal or external IP.
The application log is a single, unauthenticated text file; its integrity (no hash recorded) and completeness cannot be independently verified.
File-system timestamps on the log/scheduler/README are all identical to the capture time, so mtime-based ordering is not available as independent corroboration.
warnings: The two failed lihua logins from 198.51.100.44 at 01:47 on 2024-05-10 are a separate anomaly that should be investigated independently of the export question; they may explain how the analyst misattributed the export to lihua.
